findings.title: role="img" suppresses interactive patient cards from accessibility tree
findings.body: The root `<div className="ed-floorplan" role="img">` wraps the interactive HTML buttons. In major screen readers (like JAWS and NVDA), assigning `role="img"` to a container instructs the parser to treat the entire node as a single flat graphic, stripping all of its descendants from the accessibility tree. This completely nullifies the stated a11y benefits of migrating from Phaser to DOM buttons.
findings.recommendation: Change the root div to `role="region"` (keeping its current `aria-label`), and apply `aria-hidden="true"` or `role="img"` strictly to the underlying `<svg>` element so the overlay remains fully accessible.

findings.title: Deceased state check hard-locks case entry, breaking M&M loop
findings.body: The patient card explicitly blocks interaction via `if (!alive) return;`, which was not present in the original Phaser implementation. In the FRCEM simulation loop, when a patient dies, a clinician must still enter the case file to verify death, finalize notes, and apply the M&M folder sticker introduced in M91. This UI lock artificially prevents post-mortem case interactions.
findings.recommendation: Remove the `!alive` check blocking the `onClick` handler and drop the `aria-disabled` override. Allow players to enter deceased cases from the hub exactly as they would from the shift board.

findings.title: Absolute Y-coordinate math causes card overlap on smaller viewports
findings.body: The `top` offset for each card is calculated as a percentage of `GAME_HEIGHT` using a hardcoded 46px virtual step (`CARD_HEIGHT + CARD_GAP`). As the fluid container scales down, this percentage resolves to fewer physical pixels (e.g. a 23px step on small screens). Because the DOM cards have minimum pixel boundaries driven by font clamping and padding, they will outgrow the scaled gap and physically overlap.
findings.recommendation: Stop absolutely positioning individual cards. Instead, absolutely position a zone wrapper `<div>` matching the bay's bounding box, and render the cards inside it using standard `display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px;` to let the browser stack them safely.

findings.title: E2E test fails to capitalize on DOM visibility
findings.body: The E2E test historically only checked that the Phaser root mounted because Playwright cannot see inside a canvas. Now that patient cards are real DOM buttons, the test is missing a massive opportunity to verify the core hub loop: navigating from a patient card directly into the Encounter Screen.
findings.recommendation: Add a step to the E2E test that clicks a patient card (e.g., `await page.getByRole('button', { name: /hen-do/i }).click()`) and asserts the Encounter Screen mounts correctly.

findings.title: byBay map generation leaks into synchronous render path
findings.body: The `EdFloorplan` component reconstructs the `byBay` grouping map via a loop on every single render. Because the simulation ticks regularly, recomputing spatial mapping arrays directly inside the component's render body is structurally sloppy, even if the array is small.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the map generation in a `useMemo(() => { ... }, [patients])` block to ensure it only rebuilds when the incoming patient payload changes.

findings.title: aria-label overrides visible text, risking Voice Control failures
findings.body: The `PatientCard` overrides its accessible name entirely using `aria-label`. Under WCAG 2.5.3 (Label in Name), speech-input users who see a truncated name on screen and say 'Click [visible text]' may fail if the assistive technology interprets the overriding `aria-label` differently.
findings.recommendation: Remove `aria-label` from the button. Instead, append an `.sr-only` visually hidden `<span>` inside the button containing the extra state and triage string, so the visible `shortTitle` remains natively part of the button's text node.

overall_take: The decision to strip 1.5MB of Phaser for a static layout is mathematically and functionally correct—the live walk-around never earned its engine weight. However, the DOM transition introduces critical architecture gaps. Wrapping interactive buttons in `role="img"` completely wipes them from the accessibility tree, defeating the primary UI benefit of the refactor. Furthermore, manually calculating Y-offsets via percentage drops the ball on fluid layout; cards will physically overlap on a 13-inch laptop. But if I could only have ONE thing change before the next playtest, it's removing the `!alive` lock on deceased patients. In the NHS, when a patient dies in the bay, you don't lose the ability to look at them; you're required to go in, verify death, and finish the paperwork. Fix the FRCEM simulation logic first, then fix the CSS overlap.
